final:
I made all three edits. The third one probably won't get the running service onto 9090 by itself.

**What I changed** (checked with `git diff`; nothing is committed):

1. **`src/server.js:2`**: fixed the log message from `'listning on '` to `'listening on '`. The file still passes a syntax check.
2. **`CHANGELOG.md`**: added a `## 1.4.1` entry above `1.4.0` that says "Corrected the spelling of the startup log message."
3. **`run/live.env`**: changed `PORT=8080` to `PORT=9090`.

**Why the port change probably won't last:**
- `README.md` says a controller keeps the service matched to `deploy/service.yaml`, and `run/live.env` is regenerated from that file on each deploy. `deploy/service.yaml` still says `port: 8080`, so the next deploy will probably put `run/live.env` back to 8080. I'm going by the README here; I haven't read the controller's code.
- The comment in `live.env` says the process reads the file when it starts. So even before the next deploy, a process that's already running won't pick up 9090 until it restarts.
- I can't tell from the repository whether the service is running or which port it's on now, so I'm not claiming it listens on 9090.

**Decision for you:** to make 9090 permanent, `deploy/service.yaml` also needs `port: 9090`. I didn't change it because you didn't ask for that file. Changing it also means the controller will likely move the live service to 9090 on its next deploy, and anything that connects on 8080 will stop reaching it. Should I make that change?

input.command: git status; git log --oneline -5; ls -la; ls run; cat src/server.js; cat CHANGELOG.md; cat run/live.env
cat README.md; ls deploy; cat deploy/*; git check-ignore -v run/live.env; git ls-files

sed -i "s/'listning on '/'listening on '/" src/server.js
python3 - <<'E'
p='CHANGELOG.md';s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("# Changelog\n\n","# Changelog\n\n## 1.4.1\n- Corrected the spelling of the startup log message.\n\n",1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
E
sed -i 's/^PORT=8080$/PORT=9090/' run/live.env
git diff; node -c src/server.js 2>&1 || node --check src/server.js; echo exit=$?
